clue.text: Man calls in rowers showing over-use of voice?

indicators.note: to call someone in is to bring them inside, so the man takes the rowers into his middle

parts.note: HE is the pronoun standing for a man
oars are what rowers pull, standing for the rowers themselves

explanation.surface: Someone shouting at a rowing crew strains their throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice worn rough and croaky through strain is described this way.

clue.text: One group of detectives breaking in — serious crime

indicators.note: breaking into a word splits it open so other letters can enter

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
I is the Roman numeral for one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: A detective squad forces its way into a house where a grave offence took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' means at home, giving HOME, which I and CID break into.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a person is the gravest of offences, so this is a fair description.

clue.text: Broken rail, one resulting in a flap

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken rail on a track leads to a crash or a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges RAIL plus ONE; 'resulting in a' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged control surface on an aircraft wing is a movable flap.

clue.text: Directors hanging on to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Directors hanging on to (9)' is cut short: BOARD is directors, but nothing supplies SNOW or a definition, and no print of the full clue was found.

clue.text: More than one drink on Scottish island, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a tipple is a drink and Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland; tipple placed after Mull

explanation.surface: Ordering several drinks on a Hebridean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Mull tipple' runs together into the answer; Mull is a Scottish island off the west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifold or numerous consists of many parts, not just a single one.

clue.text: Where typing chair may be located in government office?

definitions.text: Where typing chair may be located in government office?

parts.words: Where typing chair may be located in government office?
parts.note: a typist's chair is placed beneath the person doing the typing, the office worker; read as a title, that phrase is a junior ministerial post

explanation.surface: Wondering where the typist's seat goes in a Whitehall department.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer says the chair sits beneath the clerical worker; as one term it is a junior minister in a British government department.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a junior minister or senior civil servant ranking below a department head.

clue.text: Short of time, relies on support

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them

explanation.surface: Pressed for time, someone leans on a helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' removes one T from TRUSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of beams holding up a roof, or a surgical belt, is a kind of support.

clue.text: Composer coming up in one cold vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the whole run of letters reads from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C stands for cold, as on taps
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A composer appears from inside a chilly container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole string IN + I + C + CUP backwards, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo, the Italian creator of La Boheme and Tosca, wrote operas.

clue.text: About to put up money for message

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up a word raises it so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone is about to stake cash on a communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put up' turns RE into ER; the surface reads 'About to' as 'ready to'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish and northern usage, going for the messages means running a household task or shopping trip.

clue.text: Well, we're unlikely to be taken in by her

definitions.text: Well, we're unlikely to be taken in by her

parts.words: Well, we're unlikely to be taken in by her
parts.note: taken in sounds like being fooled, but means carried into her vehicle, which a healthy person would not need

explanation.surface: A shrewd woman who will not easily fool anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a filler but means healthy: only sick or injured people are taken in by this paramedic.
explanation.definitionFit: A female crew member of an emergency medical vehicle carries patients to hospital.

clue.text: Misshapen and distorted wood

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Misshapen and distorted wood (9)': 'Misshapen' defines it, but 'distorted wood' cannot supply MALFORMED's letters (they anagram FORM, LAD, ME), so the clue appears garbled and no print of it was found.

clue.text: What may cause cruel suffering?

indicators.note: suffering suggests something tormented and twisted, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Asking what brings about painful torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'suffering' rearranges CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sore in the stomach or skin is a cause of pain.

clue.text: Copper holding a biro scribbled "animal"

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: scribbled suggests a messy scrawl, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A policeman with a ballpoint pen jots down the word animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scribbled' rearranges A + BIRO into ARIBO, which CU holds.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American reindeer is a large deer.

clue.text: Muscovite, kind of blue, lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Prussian blue is a deep blue pigment
P stands for power in physics

explanation.surface: A man from Moscow, a shade of blue, has no strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian blue' is also a cat breed, a tempting false path; the wordplay instead drops P from PRUSSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Moscow belongs to that nation.

clue.text: Woman academic has article rejected

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the short word reads in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A female lecturer has her paper turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AN into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian title for a lady, used in English for a woman.

clue.text: Hail and high seas calling for prayer

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail
maria are the dark plains on the Moon, named as seas, which are high up in the sky

explanation.surface: Stormy weather at sea makes sailors pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high seas' looks like rough water, but means the lunar maria, high above us.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic devotion to the Virgin opens with the angel's greeting.

clue.text: Tree's radioactive in Hampshire town

parts.note: the alder is a tree; with the 's it reads as alder is
hot is slang for radioactive

explanation.surface: A tree is giving off radiation in a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; the 's here is 'is', so the tree is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: This garrison town in Hampshire is home to a large army base.

clue.text: Programme on Clyde's next, perhaps

indicators.note: to programme is to arrange or set up, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: the river name with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A show about Scotland's river Clyde is coming up next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programme' looks like a TV show but is a verb rearranging ON CLYDES; the S of the possessive is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Next, as a sequence word, can be expressed as following in second place; the 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Expected to keep further account for police vehicle

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: par is the expected score in golf
and means furthermore, in addition

explanation.surface: A demand for more bookkeeping in the police motor pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A British police patrol car, once painted in blue and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British name for a patrol car used by beat officers.

clue.text: Fit nature of what could be sent in an epistolary afterthought

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is added after a letter's signature

indicators.note: what could be says these letters might be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Something fitting to add to a letter after signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' marks the anagram of the clue word 'sent', and 'in' places the result inside the postscript abbreviation; 'Fit nature' means the quality of being fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitability or appropriateness is the quality of being fit for purpose.

clue.text: Dig televised, broadcast omitting reconstructed parts of site

indicators.note: broadcast scrambles the first word, and omitting the reconstructed parts of the second strips those letters out in any order

explanation.surface: An archaeological dig shown on TV, with edited footage of the site left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: TELEVISED holds the letters of SITE plus the answer, so remove SITE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig is to search into, as in delving into a subject.

clue.text: Rope some coated with fat

indicators.note: coated with means covered by, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
any means some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Some rope covered in grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope' is the definition; 'coated with' puts the word for some inside the cooking fat, so the fat coats it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord worn round the neck or a short rope on a ship is this kind of line.

clue.text: It provides means to stay afloat

definitions.text: It provides means to stay afloat

parts.words: It provides means to stay afloat
parts.note: stay afloat suggests not sinking, but means lodging overnight on the water

explanation.surface: Something like a life jacket that keeps you buoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: A floating hotel, or a waterside hotel for boat users: a place to stay that is afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel on a moored vessel offers accommodation on the water.

clue.text: Effusion dismissed with predatory type about

parts.note: a dismissed batsman is out

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the wolf is a predator, and a predatory man is called a wolf

explanation.surface: A gushing tribute after a predator is sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns WOLF into FLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A gush or pouring out is a stream issuing forth.

clue.text: Part of corolla now plain to see

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a flower's petals is now clearly visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' is the noun, a flat grassland, not 'obvious'; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treeless grassy plain in South America, especially Venezuela, bears this Spanish name.

clue.text: Rocky height -almost at the summit there's a city

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: on top means at the summit

explanation.surface: Near the top of a craggy peak, a city comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ON TOP to ONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ontario is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: Greek character in the reserves

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve

explanation.surface: A Greek soldier serving in the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container; TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: Slough area?

parts.note: Slough reads as the Berkshire town, but here means a bog, so its area is boggy ground

explanation.surface: Asking about the district around the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but a slough is also a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy bog, and a tract of such ground is wet land.

clue.text: Catching girl going topless?

parts.note: lass is a girl

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter

explanation.surface: A girl going about without a top gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the G from GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a looped rope round a steer is a way of catching it.

clue.text: Heavy dog wrongly kept in pen

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: wrongly says these letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A heavy dog is wrongly kept in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges DOG into ODG, kept in STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is thick and filling sits heavy on the stomach; dull writing is heavy too.
